title: Module 5 Misconception Sort
intro: Decide whether each statement is true, false, or depends. These are the misconceptions that cost students points on exams.

items.s: The standard error and the standard deviation are the same thing.
items.why: The standard deviation describes spread of scores. The standard error describes spread of sample means.

items.s: Increasing sample size reduces the standard error.
items.why: SE = sigma divided by square root of n, so it shrinks as n grows.

items.s: The central limit theorem means that any sample of scores becomes normal if it is large enough.
items.why: It concerns the distribution of sample means. A large sample of scores keeps the shape of the population.

items.s: Sample means from a skewed population can still form a nearly normal distribution when n is large.
items.why: This is the central limit theorem in action.

items.s: A sample mean will equal the population mean if the sample is random.
items.why: A random sample mean is unbiased, but any single sample mean will differ from mu by sampling error.

items.s: To cut the standard error in half you need twice as many participants.
items.why: You need four times as many participants because SE depends on the square root of n.

items.s: A sample of 30 is always large enough for the central limit theorem to work.
items.why: Thirty is a common rule of thumb, but extreme skew can require more. For a normal population any n works.

items.s: The distribution of sample means has the same mean as the population.
